{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /ssd/workspace/buidlguidl/ethskills-evals-test/artifacts/standards-goal-001/2026-08-26T192634Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/.claude/skills/standards\n\n# Ethereum Standards\n\nAll of these are deployed and in production use, not proposals: **ERC-8004** (agent identity + reputation, Ethereum mainnet 2026-01-29), **x402** (HTTP payments), **EIP-3009** (gasless USDC transfers, what makes x402 practical), **EIP-7702** (smart EOAs, live with Pectra 2025-05-07). When a design needs agent discovery, third-party-attested reputation, per-call billing without accounts, or contract abilities on an address a user already owns, name the standard instead of rebuilding it — an API-key tier, a reviews table you host, or a migration to a fresh smart account are all the wrong answer to a problem one of these already solves.\n\n## ERC-8004 — agent identity and reputation\n\nTwo registries, deployed at the same pair of addresses across 40+ chains — but **the testnet set is a different pair**, and the mainnet addresses have no code on Sepolia or Base Sepolia:\n\n| | mainnets | testnets |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| IdentityRegistry (ERC-721) | `0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432` | `0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e` |\n| ReputationRegistry | `0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63` | `0x8004B663056A597Dffe9eCcC1965A193B7388713` |\n\n- `register()` mints an ERC-721. **The agentId is the tokenId the registry assigns** — never a UUID, hash, or slug you pick. Callers address the agent chain-scoped: `agentRegistry: eip155:8453:0x8004A169…` (Base) plus that `agentId`.\n- The `agentURI` (the ERC-721 tokenURI) MUST resolve to the registration file — `ipfs://`, `https://`, or a base64 `data:` URI. It carries `type: \"https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004#registration-v1\"`, `name`, `description`, `image`, a `services` array (A2A card, MCP, ENS, DID, email…), `x402Support`, `active`, a `registrations` array of `{agentId, agentRegistry}`, and optional `supportedTrust`.\n- **Bind the endpoint domain, the step that gets skipped.** If the domain serving the advertised endpoints is not the domain serving the agentURI file, publish `https://{endpoint-domain}/.well-known/agent-registration.json` with at least a `registrations` entry whose `agentRegistry` and `agentId` match the onchain agent. An A2A `agent-card.json` is a different document and does not do this. If the same domain already serves the agentURI file, control is proven there — say which of the two you are relying on rather than leaving the endpoints unbound.\n- Reputation is **client-attested**: the caller who paid posts `giveFeedback(agentId, value, valueDecimals, tag1, tag2, endpoint, feedbackURI, feedbackHash)`; the registry rejects feedback from the agent's owner and operators, so you cannot rate yourself. Values are fixed point — 99.77% uptime is `value=9977, valueDecimals=2`; 87/100 quality is `value=87, valueDecimals=0`. Read with `getSummary(agentId, clientAddresses, tag1, tag2)` and filter to clients you trust; unfiltered totals are Sybil bait.\n- The spec also defines a Validation Registry (re-execution, zkML, TEE attestation, 0–100 validator scores). It is not part of the deployed pair above — check before designing on it.\n- The contracts are live; the EIP is still **Draft**, so treat anything you have not verified onchain as movable. Registries are ERC-1967 proxies: read the implementation slot if a signature surprises you.\n\n## x402 — pay per HTTP call, no accounts\n\n`GET` → `402` + `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` → client signs → retry with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` → server verifies and settles → `200` + `PAYMENT-RESPONSE`. A facilitator (Coinbase runs a public one, anyone can run their own) performs verify/settle so the resource server never runs a node or holds gas.\n\nAmounts go on the wire in **token base units**: $0.35 USDC is `350000` (USDC has 6 decimals) — not `0.35`, not an 18-decimal figure. Native USDC on Base is `0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913`; `0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48` is mainnet USDC and `0xd9aAEc86B65D86f6A7B5B1b0c42FFA531710b6CA` is the bridged USDbC — both are the wrong contract for a Base x402 route.\n\nThe maintained TypeScript line is the scoped one: `@x402/core`, `@x402/evm`, `@x402/fetch`, `@x402/express`, with `@coinbase/x402` as the facilitator config beside it. Unscoped `x402`, `x402-fetch`, `x402-express` are frozen at 1.2.0; Go lives at `github.com/x402-foundation/x402/go/v2`. **Do not write the integration from a remembered snippet** — `x402Fetch` and `createWallet` do not exist in the scoped packages, and a one-argument `paymentMiddleware(config)` is the v1 shape. Read the installed types: on 2.x the Express middleware takes routes plus a resource server, and the fetch wrapper takes an x402 client, not a bare account.\n\n**A caller with USDC and no ETH can still pay**, because USDC implements **EIP-3009**: the client signs a `transferWithAuthorization` offchain and the server or facilitator submits it and pays the gas. That is the mechanism to name — not ERC-4337 bundlers, not an unnamed \"relayer\", not ERC-2612 permit followed by `transferFrom`.\n\n## EIP-7702 — contract code on an EOA the user already has\n\nLive on Ethereum mainnet since Pectra, **2025-05-07**. The EOA signs an authorization **with its own key** (a type `0x04` transaction) that writes a delegation designator, `0xef0100 || implementation address`, into the account. Calls to that same address then execute the implementation's code — an approve+swap batched atomically, sponsored gas, session-key auth — with the address, key, ENS name and history untouched. Deploying a fresh ERC-4337 wallet instead puts the user at a **new address**, which is what to reject whenever the existing address has to survive.\n\nThe delegation **persists**. It stays in place until a later authorization replaces it, or clears it by delegating to the zero address. It is not single-transaction-only and does not auto-revert when the batched call finishes.\n\n## Status at a glance\n\n| Standard | What | Status |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| ERC-8004 | Agent identity + reputation | Live — Ethereum mainnet 2026-01-29 (EIP still Draft) |\n| x402 | HTTP 402 payments | Live — scoped SDKs on 2.x |\n| EIP-3009 | Gasless token transfers | Live — USDC implements it |\n| EIP-7702 | Smart EOAs | Live — Pectra, 2025-05-07 |\n| ERC-4337 | Account abstraction (new account, new address) | Live, widely deployed |\n| ERC-2612 / ERC-4626 / ERC-6551 | Permit / tokenized vaults / token-bound accounts | Live |\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a63ac1fd-94ee-40e3-977f-86f9c97ae85c","uuid":"5e69527e-a627-4273-bcac-4c235064cfad","timestamp":"2026-08-26T19:26:38.673Z","isSynthetic":true}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012CA7oHRGPi56ptfoNLSGt1","type":"tool_result","content":"import { SchemeNetworkServer, MoneyParser, Network, Price, AssetAmount, PaymentRequirements } from '@x402/core/types';\nimport { A as AssetTransferMethod } from '../../types-BBC1mC8d.js';\nimport { x402ResourceServer } from '@x402/core/server';\n\n/**\n * EVM server implementation for the Exact payment scheme.\n */\ndeclare class ExactEvmScheme implements SchemeNetworkServer {\n    readonly scheme = \"exact\";\n    readonly defaultAssetTransferMethod: AssetTransferMethod;\n    readonly paymentFlows: {\n        readonly eip3009: {\n            readonly supported: readonly [\"authorization\"];\n            readonly default: \"authorization\";\n        };\n        readonly permit2: {\n            readonly supported: readonly [\"authorization\"];\n            readonly default: \"authorization\";\n        };\n    };\n    private moneyParsers;\n    /**\n     * Register a custom money parser in the parser chain.\n     * Multiple parsers can be registered - they will be tried in registration order.\n     * Each parser receives a decimal string (e.g., \"1.50\" for $1.50).\n     * If a parser returns null, the next parser in the chain will be tried.\n     * The default parser is always the final fallback.\n     *\n     * @param parser - Custom function to convert amount to AssetAmount (or null to skip)\n     * @returns The server instance for chaining\n     *\n     * @example\n     * evmServer.registerMoneyParser(async (amount, network) => {\n     *   // Custom conversion logic\n     *   if (Number(amount) > 100) {\n     *     // Use different token for large amounts\n     *     return { amount: convertToTokenAmount(String(amount), 18), asset: \"0xCustomToken\" };\n     *   }\n     *   return null; // Use next parser\n     * });\n     */\n    registerMoneyParser(parser: MoneyParser): ExactEvmScheme;\n    /**\n     * Decimals for a known default asset, or undefined.\n     *\n     * @param asset - Asset address or symbol\n     * @param network - Target network\n     * @returns Decimals when the asset is a known default; otherwise undefined\n     */\n    getAssetDecimals(asset: string, network: Network): number | undefined;\n    /**\n     * Parses a price into an asset amount.\n     * If price is already an AssetAmount, returns it directly.\n     * If price is Money (string | number), parses to decimal and tries custom parsers.\n     * Falls back to default conversion if all custom parsers return null.\n     *\n     * @param price - The price to parse\n     * @param network - The network to use\n     * @returns Promise that resolves to the parsed asset amount\n     */\n    parsePrice(price: Price, network: Network): Promise<AssetAmount>;\n    /**\n     * Build payment requirements for this scheme/network combination\n     *\n     * @param paymentRequirements - Extension keys supported by the facilitator (unused)\n     * @returns Payment requirements ready to be sent to clients\n     */\n    enhancePaymentRequirements(paymentRequirements: PaymentRequirements, supportedKind: {\n        x402Version: number;\n        scheme: string;\n        network: Network;\n        extra?: Record<string, unknown>;\n    }, extensionKeys: string[]): Promise<PaymentRequirements>;\n    /**\n     * Converts a numeric dollar amount to an AssetAmount using the default token for the network.\n     *\n     * @param amount - {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MAPm8JU52TG86983kR1rpY","type":"tool_result","content":"y cover agent discovery and trust.\n\nTo foster an open, cross-organizational agent economy, we need mechanisms for discovering and trusting agents in untrusted settings. This ERC addresses this need through three lightweight registries, which can be deployed on any L2 or on Mainnet as per-chain singletons:\n\nIdentity Registry - A minimal on-chain handle based on ERC-721 with URIStorage extension that resolves to an agent’s registration file, providing every agent with a portable, censorship-resistant identifier.\n\nReputation Registry - A standard interface for posting and fetching feedback signals. Scoring and aggregation occur both on-chain (for composability) and off-chain (for sophisticated algorithms), enabling an ecosystem of specialized services for agent scoring, auditor networks, and insurance pools.\n\nValidation Registry - Generic hooks for requesting and recording independent validators checks (e.g. stakers re-running the job, zkML verifiers, TEE oracles, trusted judges).\n\nPayments are orthogonal to this protocol and not covered here. However, examples are provided showing how x402 payments can enrich feedback signals.\n  \n    \n      \n      \n         Specification\n      \n      \n    \n\nThe key words “MUST”, “MUST NOT”, “REQUIRED”, “SHALL”, “SHALL NOT”, “SHOULD”, “SHOULD NOT”, “RECOMMENDED”, “NOT RECOMMENDED”, “MAY”, and “OPTIONAL” in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 and RFC 8174.\n  \n    \n      \n      \n         Identity Registry\n      \n      \n    \n\nThe Identity Registry uses ERC-721 with the URIStorage extension for agent registration, making all agents immediately browsable and transferable with NFTs-compliant apps. Each agent is uniquely identified globally by:\n\n\n  agentRegistry: A colon-separated string {namespace}:{chainId}:{identityRegistry} (e.g., eip155:1:0x742...) where:\n    \n      namespace: The chain family identifier (eip155 for EVM chains)\n      chainId: The blockchain network identifier\n      identityRegistry: The address where the ERC-721 registry contract is deployed\n    \n  \n  agentId: The ERC-721 tokenId assigned incrementally by the registry\n\n\nThroughout this document, tokenId in ERC-721 is referred to as agentId and tokenURI in ERC-721 is referred to as agentURI. The owner of the ERC-721 token is the owner of the agent and can transfer ownership or delegate management (e.g., updating the registration file) to operators, as supported by ERC721URIStorage.\n  \n    \n      \n      \n         Agent URI and Agent Registration File\n      \n      \n    \n\nThe agentURI MUST resolve to the agent registration file. It MAY use any URI scheme such as ipfs:// (e.g., ipfs://cid), https:// (e.g., https://example.com/agent3.json), or a base64-encoded data: URI (e.g., data:application/json;base64,eyJ0eXBlIjoi...) for fully on-chain metadata. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017Au3XXaik4GP38pZW4bEUG","type":"tool_result","content":"agentWallet is reserved and cannot be set via setMetadata() or during register() (including the metadata array overload). It represents the address where the agent receives payments and is initially set to the owner’s address. To change it, the agent owner must prove control of the new wallet by providing a valid EIP-712 signature for EOAs or ERC-1271 for smart contract wallets—by calling:\n\nfunction setAgentWallet(uint256 agentId, address newWallet, uint256 deadline, bytes calldata signature) external\n\n\nTo read and clear the currently set wallet, the following functions are exposed:\n\nfunction getAgentWallet(uint256 agentId) external view returns (address)\nfunction unsetAgentWallet(uint256 agentId) external\n\n\nWhen the agent is transferred, agentWallet is automatically cleared (effectively resetting it to the zero address) and must be re-verified by the new owner.\n  \n    \n      \n      \n         Registration\n      \n      \n    \n\nNew agents can be minted by calling one of these functions:\n\nstruct MetadataEntry {\nstring metadataKey;\nbytes metadataValue;\n}\n\nfunction register(string agentURI, MetadataEntry[] calldata metadata) external returns (uint256 agentId)\n\nfunction register(string agentURI) external returns (uint256 agentId)\n\n// agentURI is added later with setAgentURI()\nfunction register() external returns (uint256 agentId)\n\n\nThis emits one Transfer event, one MetadataSet event for the reserved agentWallet key, one MetadataSet event for each additional metadata entry (if any), and\n\nevent Registered(uint256 indexed agentId, string agentURI, address indexed owner)\n\n  \n    \n      \n      \n         Update agentURI\n      \n      \n    \n\nThe agentURI can be updated by calling the following function, which emits a URIUpdated event:\n\n\nfunction setAgentURI(uint256 agentId, string calldata newURI) external\n\nevent URIUpdated(uint256 indexed agentId, string newURI, address indexed updatedBy)\n\n\n\nIf the owner wants to store the entire registration file on-chain, the agentURI SHOULD use a base64-encoded data URI rather than a serialized JSON string:\n\ndata:application/json;base64,eyJ0eXBlIjoi...\n\n  \n    \n      \n      \n         Reputation Registry\n      \n      \n    \n\nWhen the Reputation Registry is deployed, the identityRegistry address is set via initialize(address identityRegistry_) and publicly visible by calling:\n\nfunction getIdentityRegistry() external view returns (address identityRegistry)\n\n\nThe feedback given by a clientAddress to an agent consists of a signed fixed-point value (int128) and its valueDecimals (uint8, 0-18), plus optional tag1 and tag2 (left to developers’ discretion to provide maximum on-chain composability and filtering), an endpoint URI, a file URI pointing to an off-chain JSON containing additional information, and its KECCAK-256 file hash to guarantee integrity. We suggest using IPFS or equivalent services to make feedback easily indexed by subgraphs or similar technologies. For IPFS URIs, the hash is not required.\nAll fields except value and valueDecimals are OPTIONAL, so the off-chain file is not required and can be omitted.\n  \n    \n      \n      \n         Giving Feedback\n      \n      \n    \n\nNew feedback can be added by any clientAddress calling:\n\nfunction giveFeedback(uint256 agentId, int128 value, uint8 valueDecimals, string calldata tag1, string calldata tag2, string calldata endpoint, string calldata feedbackURI, bytes32 feedbackHash) external\n\n\nThe agentId must be a validly registered agent. The valueDecimals MUST be between 0 and 18. The feedback submitter MUST NOT be the agent owner or an approved operator for agentId. tag1, tag2, endpoint, feedbackURI, and feedbackHash are OPTIONAL.\n\nWhere provided, feedbackHash is the KECCAK-256 hash (keccak256) of the content referenced by feedbackURI, enabling verifiable integrity for non-content-addressed URIs. For IPFS (or other content-addressed URIs), feedbackHash is OPTIONAL and can be omitted (e.g., set to bytes32(0)).\n\nIf the procedure succeeds, an event is emitted:\n\nevent NewFeedback(uint256 indexed agentId, address indexed clientAddress, uint64 feedbackIndex, int128 value, uint8 valueDecimals, string indexed indexedTag1, string tag1, string tag2, string endpoint, string feedbackURI, bytes32 feedbackHash)\n\n\nThe feedback fields value, valueDecimals, tag1, tag2, and isRevoked are stored in the contract storage along with the feedbackIndex (a 1-indexed counter of feedback submissions that clientAddress has given to agentId). The fields endpoint, feedbackURI, and feedbackHash are emitted but are not stored. This exposes reputation signals to any smart contract, enabling on-chain composability.\n\nWhen the feedback is given by an agent (i.e., the client is an agent), the agent SHOULD use the address set in the on-chain optional agentWallet metadata as the clientAddress, to facilitate reputation aggregation.\n  \n    \n      \n      \n         Examples of value / valueDecimals\n      \n      \n    \n\n\n  \n    \n      tag1\n      What it measures\n      Example human value\n      value\n      valueDecimals\n    \n  \n  \n    \n      starred\n      Quality rating (0-100)\n      87/100\n      87\n      0\n    \n    \n      reachable\n      Endpoint reachable (binary)\n      true\n      1\n      0\n    \n    \n      ownerVerified\n      Endpoint owned by agent owner (binary)\n      true\n      1\n      0\n    \n    \n      uptime\n      Endpoint uptime (%)\n      99.77%\n      9977\n      2\n    \n    \n      successRate\n      Endpoint success rate (%)\n      89%\n      89\n      0\n    \n    \n      responseTime\n      Response time (ms)\n      560ms\n      560\n      0\n    \n    \n      blocktimeFreshness\n      Avg block delay (blocks)\n      4 blocks\n      4\n      0\n    \n    \n      revenues\n      Cumulative revenues (e.g., USD)\n      $560\n      560\n      0\n    \n    \n      tradingYield (tag2 = day, week, month, year)\n      Yield\n      -3,2%\n      -32\n      1\n    \n  \n\n  \n    \n      \n      \n         Off-Chain Feedback File Structure\n      \n      \n    \n\nThe OPTIONAL file at the URI could look like:\n\n{\n  // MUST FIELDS\n  \"agentRegistry\": \"eip155:1:{identityRegistry}\",\n  \"agentId\": 22,\n  \"clientAddress\": \"eip155:1:{clientAddress}\",\n  \"createdAt\": \"2025-09-23T12:00:00Z\",\n  \"value\": 100,\n  \"valueDecimals\": 0,\n\n  // ALL OPTIONAL FIELDS\n  \"tag1\": \"foo\",\n  \"tag2\": \"bar\",\n  \"endpoint\": \"https://agent.example.com/GetPrice\",\n\n  \"mcp\": { \"tool\": \"ToolName\" }, // or: { \"prompt\": \"PromptName\" } / { \"resource\": \"ResourceName\" }\n\n  // A2A: see \"Context Identifier Semantics\" and Task model in the A2A {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CeRv9TnhPATb2xrDB6roZ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01D5WrWHZnuTmusKwrAYEwvw","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > server.ts <<'TSEOF'\n/**\n * forecast.example.com — service side.\n *\n * Sells a weather forecast for $0.35 USDC on Base, per call, to autonomous\n * clients that have never seen this service before.\n *\n *   discovery + trust : ERC-8004 IdentityRegistry / ReputationRegistry on Base\n *   billing           : x402 (HTTP 402 -> sign -> retry), \"exact\" scheme\n *   gas-free payment  : EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization, submitted by the facilitator\n *   gas-free rating   : EIP-7702 delegated EOA, relayed by us (optional convenience)\n *\n * See design.md for the dependency list and the publish/register checklist.\n */\n\nimport express, { type Request, type Response } from \"express\";\nimport {\n  paymentMiddleware,\n  x402ResourceServer,\n  type RoutesConfig,\n} from \"@x402/express\";\nimport { HTTPFacilitatorClient } from \"@x402/core/server\";\nimport { decodePaymentSignatureHeader } from \"@x402/core/http\";\nimport type { Network, PaymentPayload } from \"@x402/core/types\";\nimport { registerExactEvmScheme } from \"@x402/evm/exact/server\";\nimport {\n  bazaarResourceServerExtension,\n  declareDiscoveryExtension,\n} from \"@x402/extensions/bazaar\";\nimport { facilitator } from \"@coinbase/x402\";\nimport {\n  createPublicClient,\n  createWalletClient,\n  getAddress,\n  http,\n  isAddress,\n  isHex,\n  keccak256,\n  toBytes,\n  type Address,\n  type Hex,\n  type SignedAuthorization,\n} from \"viem\";\nimport { privateKeyToAccount } from \"viem/accounts\";\nimport { base } from \"viem/chains\";\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Configuration\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/** CAIP-2 id for Base mainnet. x402 addresses networks this way, not by name. */\nconst NETWORK: Network = \"eip155:8453\";\nconst CHAIN_ID = 8453;\n\n/**\n * Native USDC on Base. Not the bridged USDbC (0xd9aAEc86...) and not mainnet\n * USDC (0xA0b86991...) — both would make every payment unsettleable here.\n * Implements EIP-3009, which is what lets an ETH-less client pay.\n */\nconst USDC_BASE = getAddress(\"0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\");\n\n/** $0.35 in USDC base units. USDC has 6 decimals, so 0.35 * 10^6. */\nconst PRICE_BASE_UNITS = \"350000\";\nconst PRICE_HUMAN = \"$0.35\";\n\n/** ERC-8004 mainnet singletons. Same pair on Base as on Ethereum. */\nconst IDENTITY_REGISTRY = getAddress(\n  \"0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432\",\n);\nconst REPUTATION_REGISTRY = getAddress(\n  \"0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63\",\n);\n/** How a client names us globally: {namespace}:{chainId}:{identityRegistry}. */\nconst AGENT_REGISTRY = `eip155:${CHAIN_ID}:${IDENTITY_REGISTRY}`;\n\nconst env = process.env;\nconst PORT = Number(env.PORT ?? 8402);\nconst ORIGIN = env.PUBLIC_ORIGIN ?? \"https://forecast.example.com\";\n\n/**\n * The tokenId the IdentityRegistry assigned to us at register(). It is not a\n * slug or a uuid we chose — it is read back from the Registered event.\n */\nconst AGENT_ID = BigInt(env.AGENT_ID ?? \"0\");\n\n/** Where settlement lands. Must equal getAgentWallet(AGENT_ID) on Base. */\nconst PAY_TO = getAddress(\n  env.PAY_TO ?? \"0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000\",\n);\n\n/** ipfs:// URI of the registration file; also the ERC-721 tokenURI. */\nconst AGENT_URI = env.AGENT_URI ?? \"ipfs://bafkreiforecastexampleregistrationfileplaceholder\";\n\nconst RPC_URL = env.BASE_RPC_URL ?? \"https://mainnet.base.org\";\n\nconst publicClient = createPublicClient({\n  chain: base,\n  transport: http(RPC_URL),\n});\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Published documents\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/**\n * ERC-8004 registration file (registration-v1). The canonical copy is pinned on\n * IPFS at AGENT_URI; this identical copy is served at\n * /.well-known/agent-registration.json, which is what proves that whoever\n * controls forecast.example.com is the agent behind agentId AGENT_ID.\n *\n * Note `services[].name` / `services[].endpoint` — that is the spec's shape.\n */\nfunction registrationFile() {\n  return {\n    type: \"https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004#registration-v1\",\n    name: \"forecast.example.com\",\n    description:\n      `Point weather forecasts for any lat/lon, 0-72h ahead, as JSON. ` +\n      `${PRICE_HUMAN} per call, paid inline over x402 in USDC on Base ` +\n      `(EIP-3009, so no ETH is needed on the caller side). No account, no API ` +\n      `key, no minimum. Rate the call afterwards with giveFeedback() on the ` +\n      `ERC-8004 ReputationRegistry using tag1 \"starred\" (0-100), ` +\n      `\"successRate\" or \"responseTime\".`,\n    image: `${ORIGIN}/icon.png`,\n    services: [\n      { name: \"web\", endpoint: `${ORIGIN}/` },\n      {\n        name: \"A2A\",\n        endpoint: `${ORIGIN}/.well-known/agent-card.json`,\n        version: \"0.3.0\",\n      },\n      { name: \"HTTP\", endpoint: `${ORIGIN}/forecast`, version: \"1.0\" },\n      { name: \"x402\", endpoint: `${ORIGIN}/forecast`, version: \"2\" },\n    ],\n    x402Support: true,\n    active: true,\n    registrations: [\n      { agentId: Number(AGENT_ID), agentRegistry: AGENT_REGISTRY },\n    ],\n    supportedTrust: [\"reputation\"],\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * How to price and rate us, in machine-readable form, so a client that found\n * us through the registry can decide before spending anything.\n */\nfunction serviceManifest() {\n  return {\n    resource: `${ORIGIN}/forecast`,\n    method: \"GET\",\n    price: {\n      amount: PRICE_BASE_UNITS,\n      asset: USDC_BASE,\n      network: NETWORK,\n      decimals: 6,\n      human: PRICE_HUMAN,\n    },\n    payment: {\n      protocol: \"x402\",\n      x402Version: 2,\n      scheme: \"exact\",\n      assetTransferMethod: \"eip3009\",\n      payTo: PAY_TO,\n      facilitator: facilitator.url,\n      note:\n        \"The caller signs an EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization offchain. The \" +\n        \"facilitator submits it and pays the gas, so the caller needs USDC only.\",\n    },\n    identity: {\n      standard: \"ERC-8004\",\n      agentRegistry: AGENT_REGISTRY,\n      agentId: AGENT_ID.toString(),\n      agentURI: AGENT_URI,\n      // A client should check this equals payTo above before paying.\n      agentWalletCheck: `IdentityRegistry.getAgentWallet(${AGENT_ID})`,\n    },\n    reputation: {\n      standard: \"ERC-8004\",\n      reputationRegistry: `eip155:${CHAIN_ID}:${REPUTATION_REGISTRY}`,\n      read: \"getSummary(agentId, clientAddresses, tag1, tag2)\",\n      write: \"giveFeedback(...)\",\n      endpoint: `${ORIGIN}/forecast`,\n      tags: [\n        { tag1: \"starred\", meaning: \"quality 0-100\", valueDecimals: 0 },\n        { tag1: \"successRate\", meaning: \"percent\", valueDecimals: 0 },\n        { tag1: \"responseTime\", meaning: \"milliseconds\", valueDecimals: 0 },\n      ],\n      warning:\n        \"Pass a clientAddresses set you trust. Unfiltered totals are Sybil bait.\",\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n/** A2A card. This advertises the service; it does NOT bind the domain. */\nfunction agentCard() {\n  return {\n    protocolVersion: \"0.3.0\",\n    name: \"forecast.example.com\",\n    description: registrationFile().description,\n    url: `${ORIGIN}/a2a`,\n    preferredTransport: \"JSONRPC\",\n    version: \"1.0.0\",\n    capabilities: { streaming: false, pushNotifications: false },\n    defaultInputModes: [\"application/json\"],\n    defaultOutputModes: [\"application/json\"],\n    skills: [\n      {\n        id: \"point-forecast\",\n        name: \"Point forecast\",\n        description: \"72-hour forecast for a lat/lon.\",\n        tags: [\"weather\", \"forecast\"],\n      },\n    ],\n    // Non-standard but useful hop back to the onchain identity.\n    registrations: [\n      { agentId: Number(AGENT_ID), agentRegistry: AGENT_REGISTRY },\n    ],\n  };\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Receipts\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/**\n * A receipt links \"you paid tx X\" to \"we served you body Y\", so the rating a\n * client posts later can be checked by a third party.\n *\n * In-memory here. In production this MUST be durable and shared across\n * instances: a client that pays and then restarts our process would otherwise\n * lose the evidence for its own review. See design.md.\n */\ntype Receipt = {\n  txHash: Hex;\n  payer: Address;\n  payTo: Address;\n  amount: string;\n  asset: Address;\n  network: Network;\n  endpoint: string;\n  requestUrl: string;\n  responseHash: Hex;\n  servedAt: string;\n  latencyMs: number;\n};\n\nconst receiptsByTx = new Map<Hex, Receipt>();\n/** Bridges handler -> settle hook: EIP-3009 nonce is present in both. */\nconst pendingByNonce = new Map<\n  string,\n  { responseHash: Hex; requestUrl: string; servedAt: string; latencyMs: number }\n>();\n/** One sponsored rating per settled call. */\nconst sponsorshipByTx = new Map<Hex, \"unused\" | \"used\">();\n\nconst RECEIPT_TTL_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;\n\nfunction sweep() {\n  const cutoff = Date.now() - RECEIPT_TTL_MS;\n  for (const [tx, r] of receiptsByTx) {\n    if (Date.parse(r.servedAt) < cutoff) {\n      receiptsByTx.delete(tx);\n      sponsorshipByTx.delete(tx);\n    }\n  }\n  for (const [nonce, p] of pendingByNonce) {\n    if (Date.parse(p.servedAt) < Date.now() - 10 * 60 * 1000) {\n      pendingByNonce.delete(nonce);\n    }\n  }\n}\nsetInterval(sweep, 60_000).unref();\n\n/** The EIP-3009 authorization nonce, which identifies this one payment. */\nfunction nonceOf(payload: PaymentPayload): string | undefined {\n  const auth = (payload.payload as { authorization?: { nonce?: string } })\n    .authorization;\n  return auth?.nonce;\n}\n\nfunction payerOf(payload: PaymentPayload): Address | undefined {\n  const auth = (payload.payload as { authorization?: { from?: string } })\n    .authorization;\n  return auth?.from && isAddress(auth.from) ? getAddress(auth.from) : undefined;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// The forecast itself\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ntype Forecast = ReturnType<typeof buildForecast>;\n\nfunction buildForecast(lat: number, lon: number, hours: number) {\n  // Stand-in for the real model / upstream data call.\n  const issued = new Date();\n  const series = Array.from({ length: hours }, (_, i) => {\n    const t = new Date(issued.getTime() + (i + 1) * 3_600_000);\n    const seasonal = Math.sin(((i + lon) * Math.PI) / 12);\n    return {\n      validAt: t.toISOString(),\n      tempC: Number((14 + 8 * seasonal - Math.abs(lat) / 12).toFixed(1)),\n      precipProb: Number(Math.abs(seasonal * 0.4).toFixed(2)),\n      windMs: Number((3 + 4 * Math.abs(seasonal)).toFixed(1)),\n    };\n  });\n  return {\n    location: { lat, lon },\n    issuedAt: issued.toISOString(),\n    model: \"forecast.example.com/gfs-blend-v3\",\n    units: { tempC: \"celsius\", precipProb: \"0-1\", windMs: \"m/s\" },\n    hourly: series,\n  };\n}\n\n/** Stable digest of what we served, so the receipt is checkable. */\nfunction digest(body: unknown): Hex {\n  return keccak256(toBytes(JSON.stringify(body)));\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// x402 wiring\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/**\n * The facilitator verifies the client's EIP-3009 signature and broadcasts the\n * transferWithAuthorization, paying gas out of its own account. That is the\n * whole reason this service never runs a node, never holds ETH, and never asks\n * the caller for ETH either.\n *\n * Coinbase's public facilitator is the default; any x402 facilitator works, and\n * running our own is a config change, not a redesign.\n */\nconst facilitatorClient = new HTTPFacilitatorClient(facilitator);\n\nconst resourceServer = new x402ResourceServer(facilitatorClient);\nregisterExactEvmScheme(resourceServer, { networks: [NETWORK] });\nresourceServer.registerExtension(bazaarResourceServerExtension);\n\n/** Capture payer + response digest the moment settlement confirms. */\nresourceServer.onAfterSettle(async (ctx) => {\n  if (ctx.phase !== \"after-handler\") return;\n  const result = ctx.result;\n  if (!result.success || !result.transaction) return;\n\n  const txHash = result.transaction as Hex;\n  const nonce = nonceOf(ctx.paymentPayload as PaymentPayload);\n  const pending = nonce ? pendingByNonce.get(nonce) : undefined;\n  if (nonce) pendingByNonce.delete(nonce);\n\n  const payer =\n    (result.payer && isAddress(result.payer)\n      ? getAddress(result.payer)\n      : undefined) ?? payerOf(ctx.paymentPayload as PaymentPayload);\n  if (!payer) return;\n\n  receiptsByTx.set(txHash, {\n    txHash,\n    payer,\n    payTo: PAY_TO,\n    amount: ctx.requirements.amount,\n    asset: getAddress(ctx.requirements.asset),\n    network: ctx.requirements.network,\n    endpoint: `${ORIGIN}/forecast`,\n    requestUrl: pending?.requestUrl ?? `${ORIGIN}/forecast`,\n    responseHash: pending?.responseHash ?? (\"0x\" + \"0\".repeat(64)) as Hex,\n    servedAt: pending?.servedAt ?? new Date().toISOString(),\n    latencyMs: pending?.latencyMs ?? -1,\n  });\n  sponsorshipByTx.set(txHash, \"unused\");\n});\n\nconst routes: RoutesConfig = {\n  \"GET /forecast\": {\n    accepts: {\n      scheme: \"exact\",\n      network: NETWORK,\n      payTo: PAY_TO,\n      // Base units, not dollars: 350000 = $0.35 at 6 decimals.\n      price: { asset: USDC_BASE, amount: PRICE_BASE_UNITS },\n      maxTimeoutSeconds: 120,\n      extra: {\n        // Pin the EIP-3009 path explicitly. The Permit2 fallback would need the\n        // caller to have approved Permit2 first, which costs gas it doesn't have.\n        assetTransferMethod: \"eip3009\",\n        // EIP-712 domain of USDC on Base, needed to build the signature.\n        name: \"USD Coin\",\n        version: \"2\",\n      },\n    },\n    resource: `${ORIGIN}/forecast`,\n    description: `72-hour point weather forecast. ${PRICE_HUMAN} per call.`,\n    mimeType: \"application/json\",\n    serviceName: \"forecast.example.com\",\n    tags: [\"weather\", \"forecast\", \"erc-8004\"],\n    iconUrl: `${ORIGIN}/icon.png`,\n    // Optional index run by facilitators. Supplementary only — the registry is\n    // the discovery path that does not depend on anyone's catalog.\n    extensions: declareDiscoveryExtension({\n      input: { lat: 52.37, lon: 4.89, hours: 24 },\n      inputSchema: {\n        type: \"object\",\n        required: [\"lat\", \"lon\"],\n        properties: {\n          lat: { type: \"number\", minimum: -90, maximum: 90 },\n          lon: { type: \"number\", minimum: -180, maximum: 180 },\n          hours: { type: \"integer\", minimum: 1, maximum: 72, default: 24 },\n        },\n      },\n      output: { example: buildForecast(52.37, 4.89, 1) },\n    }),\n    /**\n     * What an unpaid caller gets back with the 402. Everything it needs to\n     * decide whether to pay: who we are onchain, and where to check our\n     * reputation without asking us.\n     */\n    unpaidResponseBody: async () => ({\n      contentType: \"application/json\",\n      body: {\n        service: \"forecast.example.com\",\n        price: PRICE_HUMAN,\n        identity: {\n          agentRegistry: AGENT_REGISTRY,\n          agentId: AGENT_ID.toString(),\n          agentURI: AGENT_URI,\n        },\n        reputation: {\n          registry: `eip155:${CHAIN_ID}:${REPUTATION_REGISTRY}`,\n          call: `getSummary(${AGENT_ID}, <clients you trust>, \"starred\", \"\")`,\n        },\n        manifest: `${ORIGIN}/.well-known/x402`,\n        sample: buildForecast(52.37, 4.89, 3),\n      },\n    }),\n  },\n};\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// App\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nconst app = express();\napp.use(express.json({ limit: \"64kb\" }));\napp.set(\"etag\", false);\n\n// --- Discovery: free, cacheable, no payment ---------------------------------\n\n/**\n * ERC-8004 endpoint domain verification. The agentURI points at IPFS, so the\n * registration file alone does not prove that this domain belongs to the agent.\n * This file, served over HTTPS from the same domain as the endpoints, is what\n * closes that gap. agent-card.json does not and cannot do this.\n */\napp.get(\"/.well-known/agent-registration.json\", (_req, res) => {\n  res.type(\"application/json\").set(\"cache-control\", \"public, max-age=300\");\n  res.json(registrationFile());\n});\n\napp.get(\"/.well-known/agent-card.json\", (_req, res) => {\n  res.type(\"application/json\").set(\"cache-control\", \"public, max-age=300\");\n  res.json(agentCard());\n});\n\napp.get(\"/.well-known/x402\", (_req, res) => {\n  res.type(\"application/json\").set(\"cache-control\", \"public, max-age=300\");\n  res.json(serviceManifest());\n});\n\n/** Our own reputation, read straight off the registry. Not our word for it. */\napp.get(\"/reputation\", async (req, res) => {\n  const clients = String(req.query.clients ?? \"\")\n    .split(\",\")\n    .map((c) => c.trim())\n    .filter((c) => isAddress(c))\n    .map((c) => getAddress(c));\n  const tag1 = String(req.query.tag1 ?? \"starred\");\n  const tag2 = String(req.query.tag2 ?? \"\");\n\n  try {\n    const [count, summaryValue, summaryValueDecimals] =\n      await publicClient.readContract({\n        address: REPUTATION_REGISTRY,\n        abi: REPUTATION_ABI,\n        functionName: \"getSummary\",\n        args: [AGENT_ID, clients, tag1, tag2],\n      });\n    res.json({\n      agentId: AGENT_ID.toString(),\n      agentRegistry: AGENT_REGISTRY,\n      reputationRegistry: REPUTATION_REGISTRY,\n      filteredBy: { clients, tag1, tag2 },\n      count: Number(count),\n      summaryValue: summaryValue.toString(),\n      summaryValueDecimals,\n      caveat:\n        \"Convenience mirror. Read getSummary() yourself with a client set you \" +\n        \"trust; do not take our word for our own score.\",\n    });\n  } catch (err) {\n    res.status(502).json({ error: \"registry read failed\", detail: String(err) });\n  }\n});\n\napp.get(\"/healthz\", (_req, res) => res.json({ ok: true }));\n\n// --- Paid route -------------------------------------------------------------\n\napp.use(paymentMiddleware(routes, resourceServer));\n\napp.get(\"/forecast\", (req: Request, res: Response) => {\n  const started = Date.now();\n  const lat = Number(req.query.lat);\n  const lon = Number(req.query.lon);\n  const hours = Math.min(72, Math.max(1, Number(req.query.hours ?? 24)));\n\n  if (!Number.isFinite(lat) || lat < -90 || lat > 90) {\n    return res.status(400).json({ error: \"lat must be a number in [-90, 90]\" });\n  }\n  if (!Number.isFinite(lon) || lon < -180 || lon > 180) {\n    return res\n      .status(400)\n      .json({ error: \"lon must be a number in [-180, 180]\" });\n  }\n\n  const forecast: Forecast = buildForecast(lat, lon, hours);\n\n  /**\n   * How to rate this call. The txHash is not known yet — settlement happens\n   * after this handler returns — so the client reads it out of the\n   * PAYMENT-RESPONSE header on this same response.\n   */\n  const body = {\n    forecast,\n    rating: {\n      standard: \"ERC-8004\",\n      chain: `eip155:${CHAIN_ID}`,\n      reputationRegistry: REPUTATION_REGISTRY,\n      call: \"giveFeedback(agentId, value, valueDecimals, tag1, tag2, endpoint, feedbackURI, feedbackHash)\",\n      agentId: AGENT_ID.toString(),\n      agentRegistry: AGENT_REGISTRY,\n      endpoint: `${ORIGIN}/forecast`,\n      suggestedTags: [\n        { tag1: \"starred\", tag2: \"\", valueDecimals: 0, range: \"0-100\" },\n        { tag1: \"responseTime\", tag2: \"\", valueDecimals: 0, unit: \"ms\" },\n      ],\n      // Receipt keyed by the settlement tx from the PAYMENT-RESPONSE header.\n      receiptUrlTemplate: `${ORIGIN}/receipts/{txHash}`,\n      feedbackFileHint: {\n        note:\n          \"Publish your feedback file to IPFS and pass feedbackHash = 0x0 \" +\n          \"(content addressing already guarantees integrity).\",\n        proofOfPayment: {\n          fromAddress: \"<your address>\",\n          toAddress: PAY_TO,\n          chainId: String(CHAIN_ID),\n          txHash: \"<from the PAYMENT-RESPONSE header>\",\n        },\n      },\n      gasless: {\n        note:\n          \"giveFeedback costs gas. If you hold no ETH, delegate your EOA with \" +\n          \"EIP-7702 and POST the call here; we relay it and pay the gas. Your \" +\n          \"address stays the same, which matters because reputation is keyed \" +\n          \"to it — a fresh ERC-4337 account would lose that link.\",\n        endpoint: `${ORIGIN}/feedback/sponsor`,\n        available: Boolean(env.RELAYER_PRIVATE_KEY),\n      },\n    },\n  };\n\n  // Stash for the settle hook, keyed by this payment's EIP-3009 nonce.\n  const header = req.header(\"payment-signature\");\n  if (header) {\n    try {\n      const payload = decodePaymentSignatureHeader(header) as PaymentPayload;\n      const nonce = nonceOf(payload);\n      if (nonce) {\n        pendingByNonce.set(nonce, {\n          responseHash: digest(body.forecast),\n          requestUrl: `${ORIGIN}${req.originalUrl}`,\n          servedAt: new Date().toISOString(),\n          latencyMs: Date.now() - started,\n        });\n      }\n    } catch {\n      // Middleware already verified the payment; this is bookkeeping only.\n    }\n  }\n\n  res.json(body);\n});\n\n// --- Receipts ---------------------------------------------------------------\n\napp.get(\"/receipts/:txHash\", (req, res) => {\n  const txHash = req.params.txHash.toLowerCase();\n  if (!isHex(txHash) || txHash.length !== 66) {\n    return res.status(400).json({ error: \"txHash must be 32 bytes hex\" });\n  }\n  const receipt = receiptsByTx.get(txHash as Hex);\n  if (!receipt) {\n    return res\n      .status(404)\n      .json({ error: \"no receipt for that settlement\", txHash });\n  }\n  res.set(\"cache-control\", \"public, max-age=86400\").json({\n    type: `${ORIGIN}/schemas/receipt-v1`,\n    ...receipt,\n    agentId: AGENT_ID.toString(),\n    agentRegistry: AGENT_REGISTRY,\n    // Ready to drop into an ERC-8004 feedback file.\n    proofOfPayment: {\n      fromAddress: receipt.payer,\n      toAddress: receipt.payTo,\n      chainId: String(CHAIN_ID),\n      txHash: receipt.txHash,\n    },\n  });\n});\n\n// --- Gas sponsorship for ratings (EIP-7702) ---------------------------------\n\nconst REPUTATION_ABI = [\n  {\n    type: \"function\",\n    name: \"getSummary\",\n    stateMutability: \"view\",\n    inputs: [\n      { name: \"agentId\", type: \"uint256\" },\n      { name: \"clientAddresses\", type: \"address[]\" },\n      { name: \"tag1\", type: \"string\" },\n      { name: \"tag2\", type: \"string\" },\n    ],\n    outputs: [\n      { name: \"count\", type: \"uint64\" },\n      { name: \"summaryValue\", type: \"int128\" },\n      { name: \"summaryValueDecimals\", type: \"uint8\" },\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    type: \"function\",\n    name: \"giveFeedback\",\n    stateMutability: \"nonpayable\",\n    inputs: [\n      { name: \"agentId\", type: \"uint256\" },\n      { name: \"value\", type: \"int128\" },\n      { name: \"valueDecimals\", type: \"uint8\" },\n      { name: \"tag1\", type: \"string\" },\n      { name: \"tag2\", type: \"string\" },\n      { name: \"endpoint\", type: \"string\" },\n      { name: \"feedbackURI\", type: \"string\" },\n      { name: \"feedbackHash\", type: \"bytes32\" },\n    ],\n    outputs: [],\n  },\n] as const;\n\nconst SPONSOR_GAS_CAP = 400_000n;\n\nconst relayerAccount = env.RELAYER_PRIVATE_KEY\n  ? privateKeyToAccount(env.RELAYER_PRIVATE_KEY as Hex)\n  : undefined;\n\nconst relayer = relayerAccount\n  ? createWalletClient({\n      account: relayerAccount,\n      chain: base,\n      transport: http(RPC_URL),\n    })\n  : undefined;\n\n/**\n * Relay a rating for a caller that holds USDC but no ETH.\n *\n * The caller has delegated its own EOA to a batch-executor implementation with\n * an EIP-7702 authorization signed by its own key. We send a transaction *to\n * the caller's address*, so the delegated code runs there and msg.sender inside\n * giveFeedback is the caller — not us. That matters twice over: the registry\n * rejects feedback from the agent's owner and operators, and reputation is\n * keyed to the caller's address, which EIP-7702 leaves untouched.\n *\n * The delegation persists after this call. It is cleared by delegating to the\n * zero address, not by the transaction ending.\n *\n * Guardrails, because paying gas for reviews of ourselves is a bias vector:\n *  - only addresses that actually paid us, one sponsorship per settled call;\n *  - value must be zero and gas is capped;\n *  - we do not inspect or gate on the rating. Sponsorship is unconditional.\n * A reader's real defence is still filtering getSummary by a trusted client\n * set. See design.md.\n */\napp.post(\"/feedback/sponsor\", async (req, res) => {\n  if (!relayer || !relayerAccount) {\n    return res.status(503).json({\n      error: \"sponsorship unavailable\",\n      hint: \"Call giveFeedback() directly, or fund your own gas.\",\n    });\n  }\n\n  const {\n    txHash,\n    authorization,\n    data,\n  }: {\n    txHash?: string;\n    authorization?: SignedAuthorization;\n    data?: string;\n  } = req.body ?? {};\n\n  if (!txHash || !isHex(txHash) || txHash.length !== 66) {\n    return res.status(400).json({ error: \"txHash of your paid call required\" });\n  }\n  const receipt = receiptsByTx.get(txHash.toLowerCase() as Hex);\n  if (!receipt) {\n    return res.status(404).json({ error: \"unknown settlement\", txHash });\n  }\n  if (sponsorshipByTx.get(receipt.txHash) !== \"unused\") {\n    return res\n      .status(409)\n      .json({ error: \"one sponsored rating per paid call\", txHash });\n  }\n  if (!data || !isHex(data)) {\n    return res.status(400).json({ error: \"data (calldata for your EOA) required\" });\n  }\n  if (authorization && authorization.chainId !== CHAIN_ID && authorization.chainId !== 0) {\n    return res\n      .status(400)\n      .json({ error: `authorization.chainId must be ${CHAIN_ID} or 0` });\n  }\n\n  // Reserve before broadcasting so a retry cannot double-spend our gas.\n  sponsorshipByTx.set(receipt.txHash, \"used\");\n\n  try {\n    // The delegated code lives at the payer's own address; that is the target.\n    const request = {\n      to: receipt.payer,\n      data: data as Hex,\n      value: 0n,\n      gas: SPONSOR_GAS_CAP,\n      ...(authorization ? { authorizationList: [authorization] } : {}),\n    } as const;\n\n    // Fail loudly before spending gas on a call that would revert anyway.\n    await publicClient.call({\n      account: relayerAccount.address,\n      to: request.to,\n      data: request.data,\n      value: 0n,\n    });\n\n    const hash = await relayer.sendTransaction(request);\n    res.json({\n      relayed: true,\n      hash,\n      note:\n        \"Confirm the NewFeedback event before treating the rating as posted. \" +\n        \"Your EIP-7702 delegation stays in place until you replace or clear it.\",\n    });\n  } catch (err) {\n    sponsorshipByTx.set(receipt.txHash, \"unused\");\n    res.status(400).json({ error: \"relay failed\", detail: String(err) });\n  }\n});\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\napp.listen(PORT, () => {\n  console.log(`forecast.example.com listening on :${PORT}`);\n  console.log(`  agent      ${AGENT_REGISTRY} / agentId ${AGENT_ID}`);\n  console.log(`  price      ${PRICE_BASE_UNITS} (${PRICE_HUMAN}) USDC ${NETWORK}`);\n  console.log(`  payTo      ${PAY_TO}`);\n  if (AGENT_ID === 0n) {\n    console.warn(\n      \"  WARNING: AGENT_ID unset. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CeRviuVwag39oPJp4tWpU","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01WypVr1rE1fCWoEbpJTvwRD","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd /ssd/workspace/buidlguidl/ethskills-evals-test/artifacts/standards-goal-001/2026-08-26T192634Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace\ncat > design.md <<'MDEOF'\n# forecast.example.com — service design\n\nSells a 72-hour point weather forecast for **$0.35 in USDC on Base**, per call,\nto autonomous agents that have never contacted us before.\n\nNothing here is bespoke. Each constraint maps onto a standard that is already\ndeployed, and the job is wiring, not invention:\n\n| Constraint | Standard | Where |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Discoverable + judgeable by a stranger, no catalog of ours | **ERC-8004** IdentityRegistry | Base `0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432` |\n| Ratings other agents can act on before choosing us | **ERC-8004** ReputationRegistry | Base `0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63` |\n| Per-call billing, no accounts / keys / balances | **x402** `exact` scheme over HTTP 402 | `@x402/express` 2.x + a facilitator |\n| Caller holds USDC but no ETH | **EIP-3009** `transferWithAuthorization` | native USDC on Base implements it |\n| Caller also has no gas to *rate* us | **EIP-7702** delegated EOA + our relayer | optional convenience endpoint |\n\nVerified against the live contracts on Base while writing this: both registry\naddresses hold ERC-1967 proxy code, `IdentityRegistry.name()` is `AgentIdentity`\n(`AGENT`, `getVersion() == 2.0.0`), and `ReputationRegistry.getIdentityRegistry()`\nreturns the identity registry above. USDC on Base reports `name = \"USD Coin\"`,\n`version = \"2\"`, `decimals = 6`.\n\n---\n\n## 1. The flow, end to end\n\n```\n                         ┌──────────────────────────────────┐\n   (a) discover          │ ERC-8004 IdentityRegistry (Base) │\n   ────────────────────► │   tokenURI(agentId) -> agentURI  │\n                         └───────────────┬──────────────────┘\n                                         │ ipfs://<cid>\n                         ┌───────────────▼──────────────────┐\n   (b) read reg. file    │  registration file (registration-v1)\n                         │  services[], x402Support, registrations[]\n                         └───────────────┬──────────────────┘\n                                         │ endpoint domain\n   (c) verify the domain  ───► GET https://forecast.example.com/.well-known/agent-registration.json\n                                         │\n   (d) judge us           ───► ReputationRegistry.getSummary(agentId, trustedClients, \"starred\", \"\")\n                                         │\n   (e) GET /forecast      ───► 402 + PAYMENT-REQUIRED   (350000 USDC base units, eip3009)\n   (f) sign EIP-3009      ───► retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE\n   (g) facilitator verifies, submits transferWithAuthorization, pays the gas\n   (h) 200 + forecast + PAYMENT-RESPONSE (txHash)\n   (i) GET /receipts/{txHash}\n   (j) giveFeedback(agentId, 92, 0, \"starred\", \"\", endpoint, feedbackURI, 0x0)\n       — directly, or relayed through /feedback/sponsor if the caller has no ETH\n```\n\nNo human anywhere in (a)–(j). Every document a client needs is machine-readable\nJSON with a declared `type`, and every trust signal is read from a public\ncontract rather than from us.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Discovery, and why it doesn't route through anything we own\n\n**The anchor is the ERC-8004 IdentityRegistry**, an ERC-721 singleton deployed at\nthe same address across 40+ chains. We call `register(agentURI)` once; it mints a\ntoken and the registry assigns the `agentId` — **the agentId is the tokenId**, not\na slug, uuid or hash we picked. A client names us globally as:\n\n```\nagentRegistry : eip155:8453:0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432\nagentId       : <the tokenId from the Registered event>\n```\n\nThat pair is enough for anyone with a Base RPC endpoint to find us: enumerate\n`Registered` events, or resolve `tokenURI(agentId)`. It is a neutral public\ncontract, so this satisfies \"not a catalog you own or operate\" in the strong\nsense — we cannot delist a competitor, and nobody can delist us.\n\n**Three things are published, in three different places:**\n\n| Document | Where | Purpose |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Registration file (`registration-v1`) | IPFS, pinned; CID is the `agentURI` | The canonical record `tokenURI` resolves to |\n| Same file, byte-identical | `https://forecast.example.com/.well-known/agent-registration.json` | **Endpoint domain verification** |\n| A2A agent card | `https://forecast.example.com/.well-known/agent-card.json` | Task-level interface description |\n\nThe registration file's shape is fixed by the spec — note that `services`\nentries use `name` / `endpoint`, not `type` / `serviceEndpoint`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004#registration-v1\",\n  \"name\": \"forecast.example.com\",\n  \"description\": \"…what it does, pricing, how to pay, how to rate…\",\n  \"image\": \"https://forecast.example.com/icon.png\",\n  \"services\": [\n    { \"name\": \"web\",  \"endpoint\": \"https://forecast.example.com/\" },\n    { \"name\": \"A2A\",  \"endpoint\": \"https://forecast.example.com/.well-known/agent-card.json\", \"version\": \"0.3.0\" },\n    { \"name\": \"HTTP\", \"endpoint\": \"https://forecast.example.com/forecast\", \"version\": \"1.0\" },\n    { \"name\": \"x402\", \"endpoint\": \"https://forecast.example.com/forecast\", \"version\": \"2\" }\n  ],\n  \"x402Support\": true,\n  \"active\": true,\n  \"registrations\": [\n    { \"agentId\": 4242, \"agentRegistry\": \"eip155:8453:0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432\" }\n  ],\n  \"supportedTrust\": [\"reputation\"]\n}\n```\n\n### The domain binding — the step that usually gets skipped\n\n`agentURI` points at IPFS, so the registration file by itself proves nothing about\nwho controls `forecast.example.com`. Anyone can list someone else's domain in\n`services[]`. **We rely on the `.well-known/agent-registration.json` route**: it is\nserved over HTTPS from the same domain as the advertised endpoints and carries a\n`registrations` entry whose `agentRegistry` and `agentId` match the onchain agent.\nA client that fetches it and finds a match may treat the domain as verified.\n\nThe A2A `agent-card.json` is a **different document and does not do this**, even\nthough we mirror the `registrations` array into it as a convenience hop back to\nthe chain. Do not substitute one for the other.\n\n(The alternative — setting `agentURI` to `https://forecast.example.com/agent.json`\n— would prove domain control at the `agentURI` itself and make the `.well-known`\nfile unnecessary. We chose IPFS because a content-addressed registration file\nsurvives our infrastructure and cannot be silently rewritten. The cost is exactly\none extra published file.)\n\n### Binding payTo onchain\n\n`IdentityRegistry` reserves the metadata key `agentWallet`. It starts as the\nowner's address; changing it requires an EIP-712 signature from the new wallet\n(ERC-1271 for contract wallets), via\n`setAgentWallet(agentId, newWallet, deadline, signature)`. We point it at the\naddress in our x402 `payTo`, which gives a client a cheap anti-phishing check:\n\n```\nIdentityRegistry.getAgentWallet(agentId) == accepts[0].payTo   ?\n```\n\nIf a hijacked DNS record or a spoofed 402 swaps in a different `payTo`, that check\nfails. Note: **transferring the agent NFT clears `agentWallet`** and the new owner\nmust re-verify it, so a client seeing `0x0` should treat the binding as absent\nrather than as a failure.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Billing: x402 + EIP-3009\n\n`GET /forecast` is wrapped in `paymentMiddleware(routes, resourceServer)` from\n`@x402/express` (the scoped 2.x line — the unscoped `x402-express` is frozen at\n1.2.0, and its one-argument `paymentMiddleware(config)` shape does not apply here).\n\nAn unpaid request gets `402` with a `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"scheme\": \"exact\",\n  \"network\": \"eip155:8453\",\n  \"amount\": \"350000\",\n  \"asset\":  \"0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\",\n  \"payTo\":  \"0x…\",\n  \"maxTimeoutSeconds\": 120,\n  \"extra\": { \"assetTransferMethod\": \"eip3009\", \"name\": \"USD Coin\", \"version\": \"2\" }\n}\n```\n\nThree details that are easy to get wrong and expensive to get wrong:\n\n- **`amount` is in token base units.** $0.35 with 6-decimal USDC is `350000`.\n  Not `0.35`, and not an 18-decimal figure.\n- **`asset` is native USDC on Base.** `0xA0b86991…` is Ethereum mainnet USDC and\n  `0xd9aAEc86…` is bridged USDbC; either would make every payment unsettleable.\n- **`assetTransferMethod` is pinned to `eip3009`.** The `exact` scheme also has a\n  Permit2 path, which requires the payer to have approved Permit2 first — an\n  onchain transaction, which needs ETH the caller does not have. Leaving it to\n  the default happens to work for Base USDC today; pinning it means a future\n  default change cannot quietly break the ETH-less caller.\n\n### Why the caller needs no ETH\n\nUSDC implements **EIP-3009**. The client signs a `transferWithAuthorization`\nmessage offchain — `from`, `to`, `value`, `validAfter`, `validBefore`, `nonce` —\nand sends it in the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header. The **facilitator** submits that\nauthorization onchain and pays the gas from its own account, then reports back\n`{ success, payer, transaction }`, which the middleware echoes in\n`PAYMENT-RESPONSE`.\n\nThis is the mechanism, and it is worth naming precisely: not ERC-4337 bundlers,\nnot an unnamed \"relayer\", and not ERC-2612 `permit` followed by `transferFrom`.\nThe caller needs USDC and a signing key. That is all.\n\nWe default to Coinbase's public facilitator\n(`https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402`, needs CDP API credentials) but\n`X402_FACILITATOR_URL` switches to any other, including one we run ourselves. That\nis a config change, not a redesign — the resource server never touches a node.\n\n### Constraint compliance\n\n- No accounts, no API keys, no subscriptions — the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header\n  *is* the authorization, one per call.\n- No pre-funded balances held by us — settlement moves USDC directly from payer\n  to `payTo`. We never custody a client's funds, so there is nothing to refund\n  and no invoice to reconcile.\n- Failed work isn't charged: the middleware cancels settlement when the handler\n  returns ≥ 400, so a caller who sends `lat=999` pays nothing.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Reputation\n\nFeedback is **client-attested**. The caller who paid posts it themselves:\n\n```solidity\ngiveFeedback(\n  uint256 agentId, int128 value, uint8 valueDecimals,\n  string tag1, string tag2, string endpoint,\n  string feedbackURI, bytes32 feedbackHash\n)\n```\n\nThe registry rejects feedback from the agent's owner and its approved operators,\nso **we cannot rate ourselves**, and we cannot delete or edit a rating (only the\nclient can `revokeFeedback`; anyone may `appendResponse` to add context, which is\nhow we would answer an unfair review).\n\nValues are fixed point. We advertise the spec's standard tags rather than\ninventing our own, so our scores are comparable with every other ERC-8004 agent:\n\n| `tag1` | Meaning | Example | `value` | `valueDecimals` |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| `starred` | quality 0–100 | 92/100 | `92` | `0` |\n| `successRate` | percent | 89% | `89` | `0` |\n| `responseTime` | milliseconds | 560 ms | `560` | `0` |\n| `uptime` | percent | 99.77% | `9977` | `2` |\n\nReaders use:\n\n```solidity\ngetSummary(agentId, clientAddresses, tag1, tag2)\n  returns (uint64 count, int128 summaryValue, uint8 summaryValueDecimals)\n```\n\n**`clientAddresses` must be non-empty — the contract reverts otherwise, by\ndesign.** An unfiltered average is trivially inflated by an agent rating itself\nfrom throwaway addresses. A client should pass a set whose judgement it trusts\n(peers, an aggregator it subscribes to, agents it has transacted with);\n`getClients(agentId)` enumerates everyone who has rated us, as a starting point.\nOur `/reputation` route mirrors this read for convenience and says outright that\nit should not be believed over a direct read.\n\n### Tying the rating to a real payment\n\nThe service mints a **receipt** when settlement confirms, keyed by the settlement\ntx hash, joining \"you paid tx X\" to \"we served you body Y\":\n\n```json\n{\n  \"txHash\": \"0x…\", \"payer\": \"0x…\", \"payTo\": \"0x…\",\n  \"amount\": \"350000\", \"asset\": \"0x8335…\", \"network\": \"eip155:8453\",\n  \"endpoint\": \"https://forecast.example.com/forecast\",\n  \"requestUrl\": \"…?lat=52.37&lon=4.89\", \"responseHash\": \"0x…keccak256\",\n  \"servedAt\": \"…\", \"latencyMs\": 41,\n  \"proofOfPayment\": { \"fromAddress\": \"0x…\", \"toAddress\": \"0x…\", \"chainId\": \"8453\", \"txHash\": \"0x…\" }\n}\n```\n\n`proofOfPayment` is the spec's own field for exactly this, and drops straight into\nthe client's offchain feedback file. The client publishes that file to IPFS,\npasses the `ipfs://` URI as `feedbackURI`, and may pass `feedbackHash = 0x0` —\ncontent addressing already guarantees integrity, so the hash is only needed for\nmutable `https://` URIs.\n\nThe tx hash is not in the 200 body: settlement happens *after* the handler runs,\nso the client reads it from the `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` header of that same response\nand then fetches `/receipts/{txHash}`.\n\n### Rating without gas — EIP-7702\n\n`giveFeedback` is an onchain call and costs gas, which reintroduces exactly the\nproblem EIP-3009 solved for payment. A caller with USDC and no ETH would be\nunable to rate us, which breaks the \"no step requires a human\" constraint at the\nlast step.\n\n`POST /feedback/sponsor` closes it. The client delegates its **own EOA** with an\nEIP-7702 authorization signed by its own key (a type `0x04` transaction writes\n`0xef0100 || implementation` into the account), and hands us the signed\nauthorization plus the calldata. We send a transaction **to the client's own\naddress**, so the delegated code executes there and `msg.sender` inside\n`giveFeedback` is the client — not us. We only pay the gas.\n\nWhy EIP-7702 specifically and not ERC-4337: **reputation is keyed to the client's\naddress**. Deploying a fresh smart account would put the client at a *new*\naddress, orphaning every rating it has given and every reputation it has built as\na client. EIP-7702 keeps the address, key, ENS name and history intact. That is\nthe whole reason to reach for it here.\n\nTwo properties to be explicit about:\n\n- **The delegation persists.** It stays until a later authorization replaces it,\n  or clears it by delegating to the zero address. It does not auto-revert when\n  the batched call finishes. Clients should know they are changing their account,\n  not borrowing a one-shot.\n- **Us paying gas for reviews of ourselves is a bias vector.** Mitigations: we\n  sponsor only addresses that actually paid us, at most once per settled call;\n  `value` must be zero and gas is capped; and we do not inspect or gate on the\n  rating — sponsorship is unconditional. None of that is airtight, and it isn't\n  meant to be. The real defence is the one the spec builds in: readers filter\n  `getSummary` by a client set they trust, which makes buying ratings from\n  addresses nobody trusts worthless. Clients that hold ETH should just call\n  `giveFeedback` directly and skip us entirely.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Dependencies\n\n### Onchain (Base mainnet, `eip155:8453`)\n\n| Contract | Address | Used for | Failure mode |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| IdentityRegistry (ERC-721) | `0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432` | `register`, `tokenURI`, `setAgentURI`, `setAgentWallet`, `getAgentWallet` | Discovery breaks; paid calls still work for clients that already know us |\n| ReputationRegistry | `0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63` | `giveFeedback`, `getSummary`, `getClients`, `appendResponse` | New ratings can't be posted; existing ones stay readable |\n| USDC (native, Base) | `0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913` | EIP-3009 settlement asset | Payment stops entirely |\n\nBoth registries are **ERC-1967 proxies**; read the implementation slot if a\nsignature ever surprises you. On Base today they point at\n`0x7274e874CA62410a93Bd8bf61c69d8045E399c02` and\n`0x16e0FA7f7C56B9a767E34B192B51f921BE31dA34`.\n\n**Testnet uses a different pair** — `0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e`\nand `0x8004B663056A597Dffe9eCcC1965A193B7388713`. The mainnet addresses have no\ncode on Base Sepolia, so a staging deploy that reuses them fails at the first\ncall. Base Sepolia USDC is `0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e`.\n\nThe ERC-8004 contracts are live and in production use; the EIP itself is still\n**Draft**. Treat anything not verified against the deployed bytecode as movable.\n\nThe spec also defines a **Validation Registry** (re-execution, zkML, TEE\nattestation, 0–100 validator scores). It is *not* part of the deployed pair above\n— check for a deployment before designing on it. We list only `\"reputation\"` in\n`supportedTrust` for that reason.\n\n### Offchain\n\n| Dependency | Role | If it fails |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| x402 facilitator | verify + settle, pays gas for EIP-3009 | No settlement → no revenue. Swap via `X402_FACILITATOR_URL`; run our own for full control |\n| Base RPC | `getSummary`, sponsorship pre-flight, relay | `/reputation` degrades to 502; paid calls unaffected (settlement is the facilitator's job) |\n| IPFS pinning | hosts the registration file at `agentURI` | `tokenURI` dangles. Pin on ≥2 services; the `.well-known` copy is a live fallback |\n| DNS + TLS for `forecast.example.com` | endpoints and domain verification | Domain binding fails; a careful client declines to trust the endpoints |\n| Relayer key + ETH on Base | EIP-7702 gas sponsorship | `/feedback/sponsor` returns 503; clients with ETH are unaffected |\n| Receipt store | joins payment ↔ delivery | See below |\n| Facilitator \"bazaar\" index | supplementary discovery | Nothing breaks — the registry is the primary path |\n\n**The receipt store is the one piece that must be durable and shared across\ninstances.** The reference implementation uses an in-memory `Map`, which is\nwrong for production: a client that pays and then hits a restarted process loses\nthe evidence for its own review, and the sponsorship \"once per settled call\"\ncounter resets. Use Postgres or Redis with a TTL ≥ the window in which a client\nmay rate (we keep 7 days).\n\nTwo smaller caveats worth carrying forward:\n\n- Sponsorship marks a receipt used *before* broadcasting and rolls back on error.\n  If `sendTransaction` throws after the transaction actually reached the mempool,\n  the rollback allows one duplicate gas spend. Bounded and cheap; make it exact\n  with a durable store if it matters.\n- The sponsorship pre-flight `eth_call` only catches reverts once the delegation\n  is already installed. An EOA with no code accepts any calldata, so a first-time\n  authorization landing in the same transaction cannot be simulated.\n\n### npm\n\n`@x402/core`, `@x402/evm`, `@x402/express`, `@x402/extensions` (2.23.0),\n`@coinbase/x402`, `express` 5, `viem` 2. The unscoped `x402*` packages are frozen\nat 1.2.0 and are a different API.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Checklist: what must exist before anyone can find us\n\n1. **Fund an owner EOA on Base** with a little ETH — enough for `register`,\n   `setAgentWallet`, and any later `setAgentURI`. One-off.\n2. **Write the registration file and pin it to IPFS.** Leave `registrations[]`\n   empty for now; you don't have an agentId yet.\n3. **`register(agentURI)`** on `0x8004A169…`. Read the `agentId` out of the\n   `Registered(agentId, agentURI, owner)` event — the registry assigns it. Set\n   it as `AGENT_ID` in the service environment.\n4. **Re-pin the registration file** with `registrations[]` now filled in\n   (`{ agentId, agentRegistry: \"eip155:8453:0x8004A169…\" }`), and\n   **`setAgentURI(agentId, newCid)`**. Steps 2–4 are one bootstrapping cycle; the\n   `register()` overload that takes no URI lets you invert the order instead.\n5. **`setAgentWallet(agentId, payTo, deadline, signature)`** with an EIP-712\n   signature from the `payTo` key, so `getAgentWallet` matches what the 402\n   advertises.\n6. **Deploy the service** with `AGENT_ID`, `PAY_TO`, `AGENT_URI`,\n   `PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, and facilitator credentials, serving:\n   - `GET /.well-known/agent-registration.json` — the domain binding\n   - `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` — A2A card\n   - `GET /.well-known/x402` — price, payTo, identity and reputation pointers\n   - `GET /forecast` — the paid route\n   - `GET /receipts/:txHash`, `GET /reputation`, `POST /feedback/sponsor`\n7. **DNS + TLS** for `forecast.example.com`. The domain binding is only\n   meaningful over HTTPS.\n8. **Facilitator credentials** (CDP API key for Coinbase's, or point\n   `X402_FACILITATOR_URL` at your own).\n9. *Optional:* fund a relayer key for EIP-7702 sponsorship. Without it,\n   `/feedback/sponsor` reports itself unavailable and clients with ETH still rate\n   us normally.\n10. *Optional:* the route declares a `bazaar` discovery extension, so facilitators\n    that run an index can list it. Supplementary — a catalog we don't operate,\n    and not the path a stranger must depend on.\n\nNothing in this list requires a human on the **client** side. Steps 1–9 are our\none-time operator setup; after that the whole discover → judge → pay → serve →\nrate loop runs agent-to-agent.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Running it\n\n```bash\nnpm install\nAGENT_ID=4242 \\\nPAY_TO=0x… \\\nAGENT_URI=ipfs://bafy… \\\nPUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://forecast.example.com \\\nCDP_API_KEY_ID=… CDP_API_KEY_SECRET=… \\\nnpx tsx server.ts\n```\n\nVerified locally against a stub facilitator: the 402 carries `amount: \"350000\"`,\nnative Base USDC, `assetTransferMethod: \"eip3009\"` and the USDC EIP-712 domain;\na retry with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` returns 200 plus `PAYMENT-RESPONSE`; the receipt\nappears at `/receipts/{txHash}` with a populated `proofOfPayment`; and\n`/reputation` reads `getSummary` off the real ReputationRegistry on Base mainnet.\nMDEOF\nwc -l design.md"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1084,"cache_read_input_tokens":135761,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1084},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a63ac1fd-94ee-40e3-977f-86f9c97ae85c","uuid":"eacb37cb-32a1-4d51-888c-08c9c43e017f","timestamp":"2026-08-26T19:41:36.373Z","request_id":"req_011CeRvitSC3Eeq3iyPUmAGs"}

Not the bridged USDbC (0xd9aAEc86...) and not mainnet\n * USDC (0xA0b86991...) — both would make every payment unsettleable here.\n * Implements EIP-3009, which is what lets an ETH-less client pay.\n */\nconst USDC_BASE = getAddress(\"0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\");\n\n/** $0.35 in USDC base units. USDC has 6 decimals, so 0.35 * 10^6. */\nconst PRICE_BASE_UNITS = \"350000\";\nconst PRICE_HUMAN = \"$0.35\";\n\n/** ERC-8004 mainnet singletons. Same pair on Base as on Ethereum. */\nconst IDENTITY_REGISTRY = getAddress(\n  \"0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432\",\n);\nconst REPUTATION_REGISTRY = getAddress(\n  \"0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63\",\n);\n/** How a client names us globally: {namespace}:{chainId}:{identityRegistry}. */\nconst AGENT_REGISTRY = `eip155:${CHAIN_ID}:${IDENTITY_REGISTRY}`;\n\nconst env = process.env;\nconst PORT = Number(env.PORT ?? 8402);\nconst ORIGIN = env.PUBLIC_ORIGIN ?? \"https://forecast.example.com\";\n\n/**\n * The tokenId the IdentityRegistry assigned to us at register(). It is not a\n * slug or a uuid we chose — it is read back from the Registered event.\n */\nconst AGENT_ID = BigInt(env.AGENT_ID ?? \"0\");\n\n/** Where settlement lands. Must equal getAgentWallet(AGENT_ID) on Base. */\nconst PAY_TO = getAddress(\n  env.PAY_TO ?? \"0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000\",\n);\n\n/** ipfs:// URI of the registration file; also the ERC-721 tokenURI. */\nconst AGENT_URI = env.AGENT_URI ?? \"ipfs://bafkreiforecastexampleregistrationfileplaceholder\";\n\nconst RPC_URL = env.BASE_RPC_URL ?? \"https://mainnet.base.org\";\n\n/** Only the two ReputationRegistry functions this service touches. */\nconst REPUTATION_ABI = [\n  {\n    type: \"function\",\n    name: \"getSummary\",\n    stateMutability: \"view\",\n    inputs: [\n      { name: \"agentId\", type: \"uint256\" },\n      { name: \"clientAddresses\", type: \"address[]\" },\n      { name: \"tag1\", type: \"string\" },\n      { name: \"tag2\", type: \"string\" },\n    ],\n    outputs: [\n      { name: \"count\", type: \"uint64\" },\n      { name: \"summaryValue\", type: \"int128\" },\n      { name: \"summaryValueDecimals\", type: \"uint8\" },\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    type: \"function\",\n    name: \"giveFeedback\",\n    stateMutability: \"nonpayable\",\n    inputs: [\n      { name: \"agentId\", type: \"uint256\" },\n      { name: \"value\", type: \"int128\" },\n      { name: \"valueDecimals\", type: \"uint8\" },\n      { name: \"tag1\", type: \"string\" },\n      { name: \"tag2\", type: \"string\" },\n      { name: \"endpoint\", type: \"string\" },\n      { name: \"feedbackURI\", type: \"string\" },\n      { name: \"feedbackHash\", type: \"bytes32\" },\n    ],\n    outputs: [],\n  },\n] as const;\n\nconst publicClient = createPublicClient({\n  chain: base,\n  transport: http(RPC_URL),\n});\n\n/**\n * Normalise an address that arrived over the wire.\n *\n * viem's isAddress() defaults to strict checksum validation, which rejects a\n * mixed-case address whose EIP-55 checksum is wrong even though the bytes are\n * fine. Payers and query params are not guaranteed to be checksummed, Both deliverables are in the workspace, typechecked, and smoke-tested end to end.\n\n## What I built\n\n**`design.md`** (432 lines) — architecture, the full onchain/offchain dependency table, and a publish/register checklist.\n\n**`server.ts`** (810 lines) — Express server, typechecks clean, verified against a stub facilitator.\n\n## Standard per constraint\n\n| Constraint | Answer |\n|---|---|\n| Stranger discovers + judges us, no catalog of ours | **ERC-8004** IdentityRegistry `0x8004A169…` on Base — a neutral public ERC-721 singleton. `register(agentURI)` mints; the registry assigns the `agentId` |\n| Per call, no accounts/keys/balances | **x402** `exact` scheme, `@x402/express` 2.x. The `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header *is* the authorization |\n| USDC but no ETH | **EIP-3009** `transferWithAuthorization` — client signs offchain, facilitator submits and pays gas |\n| Ratings others can act on | **ERC-8004** ReputationRegistry, client-attested. The registry rejects feedback from our owner/operators, so we can't rate ourselves |\n| No humans | Every document is typed JSON; every trust signal reads off a contract |\n\n## Things I want to flag\n\n**The domain binding.** `agentURI` points at IPFS, so the registration file alone proves nothing about who controls `forecast.example.com`. The server publishes `/.well-known/agent-registration.json` from the endpoint domain with matching `registrations`. The A2A `agent-card.json` is a different document and does not do this — design.md says so explicitly.\n\n**A gap in the constraint set.** `giveFeedback` costs gas, so an ETH-less caller can pay but can't rate — breaking \"no step requires a human\" at the last step. I closed it with **EIP-7702**: the client delegates its own EOA, we relay to that address so `msg.sender` is the client, and we pay gas. ERC-4337 would be wrong here specifically because reputation is keyed to the client's address and a fresh smart account is a *new* address. design.md is candid that us sponsoring gas for our own reviews is a bias vector, lists the guardrails, and says the real defence is readers filtering `getSummary` by a trusted client set.\n\n**Two bugs found by testing, both same root cause.** viem's `isAddress` defaults to strict EIP-55 checksum validation, which silently dropped a payer whose address wasn't canonically cased — killing receipt creation and reputation filters. Fixed with a `toAddress()` helper.\n\n## Verified live, not remembered\n\nI read the installed `@x402/*` types rather than writing from a snippet, and pulled the verified registry ABIs off Sourcify. Confirmed on Base mainnet: both registries hold ERC-1967 proxy code, `IdentityRegistry.name()` is `AgentIdentity` (v2.0.0), `ReputationRegistry.getIdentityRegistry()` points back correctly, and USDC reports `name \"USD Coin\"`, `version \"2\"`, 6 decimals. The `/reputation` route did a real `getSummary` read against Base mainnet during testing.\n\nThe 402 carries `amount: \"350000\"` (base units, not `0.35`), native Base USDC, and `assetTransferMethod: \"eip3009\"` pinned explicitly — the Permit2 fallback would need a prior approval the ETH-less caller can't afford.\n\nOne note: `npm start` needs `CDP_API_KEY_ID`/`CDP_API_KEY_SECRET` for Coinbase's facilitator; without them startup logs a 401 on `getSupported` and paid routes 500. `X402_FACILITATOR_URL` switches to any other facilitator."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2419,"cache_read_input_tokens":148242,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2419},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a63ac1fd-94ee-40e3-977f-86f9c97ae85c","uuid":"4590c618-c998-4cc5-bb19-ee04ce18ffa8","timestamp":"2026-08-26T19:42:44.602Z","request_id":"req_011CeRvvz9Kxcs4wBWjRNm1b"}
